summary: XRD analysis across the paper demonstrates that purification of CsPbBrxI3-x nanocrystal thin films with increasingly polar antisolvents (from methyl acetate to acetone to butanol) results in systematic shifts of the (100), (200), and (300) diffraction peaks to higher 2θ values, indicating a reduction in lattice parameter. This trend is consistent with the removal of larger iodide anions and a relative enrichment of bromide in the perovskite lattice. However, quantitative details such as FWHM and explicit phase identification are not provided, limiting the ability to assess crystallinity or phase purity.
experimental_variables: Type of antisolvent used for purification (none, methyl acetate, acetone, butanol)

key_findings.finding: Diffraction peaks (100, 200, 300) shift to higher 2θ values as the polarity of the antisolvent increases.
Peak positions for the (100), (200), and (300) reflections are progressively higher for MeOAc, acetone, and butanol compared to the original sample.
All XRD peaks are broad, suggesting nanocrystalline character across all samples.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The systematic shift of XRD peaks to higher 2θ values with more polar antisolvents indicates a reduction in lattice parameter, likely due to the removal of larger iodide anions and enrichment of bromide in the perovskite lattice.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: The trend of increasing 2θ for all major peaks with more polar antisolvents, as well as the explicit mention in the caption and text, supports the interpretation that lattice contraction occurs due to halide composition change.

citations.evidence: Diffraction peaks shift to higher 2θ with more polar antisolvent
X-ray diffraction patterns of pristine and purified NC thin films on glass substrates.

XRD measurements showed that the (100) and (200) peaks of the NCs shifted toward higher 2θ values as the antisolvent polarity was increased (Figure 1e ), showing that the lattice parameter was reduced, which correlates with the removal of the larger I - anions.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The broadness of all XRD peaks across samples suggests that the nanocrystals remain small and nanocrystalline regardless of purification method.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: All samples are reported to have broad peaks, and no significant change in peak width is noted across conditions, indicating consistently small crystallite size.

scientific_interpretation.claim: No new crystalline phases are detected after antisolvent purification; only peak positions shift, suggesting the perovskite structure is retained.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: No additional peaks or phase assignments are reported, and only the positions of existing peaks change with treatment.

limitations.claim: No quantitative FWHM or crystallite size analysis is provided, limiting assessment of changes in crystallinity or size.
No explicit phase identification or Rietveld refinement is reported, so minor impurity phases or subtle structural changes cannot be ruled out.
Peak intensity changes are not discussed or quantified, so possible changes in preferred orientation or crystallinity cannot be evaluated.
Only one figure with XRD data is provided, limiting the ability to assess reproducibility or trends across multiple experimental series.

citations.evidence: Figure 1. (e) X-ray diffraction patterns of pristine and purified NC thin films on glass substrates.
